exceptions.reason: TRUE OF THE CARD-MODE VARIANT ONLY. The wide layout is a real <table> with role="grid", one roving tab stop and a cursor that starts on the first column header. Below --bp-md the table renders one card per row -- a list, not a grid -- and a card whose `TableRow` carries a `click` has no keyboard route at all: it is a <div> with onClick and cursor:pointer. The obvious fix is invalid ARIA, which is why it is recorded rather than done: tabIndex={0} plus role="button" cannot go on a card that also contains the consumer's own buttons, and a column marked mobileLayout: 'block' is exactly where they go. The other requirements of this pattern are vacuous rather than unmet in card mode -- the grid pattern's subject is the grid element, and there is no grid element there -- but this one costs a keyboard user a capability they have in the wide layout, so it is an exception and not a silence. Separately, and in BOTH layouts: a cell whose content the consumer draws -- a Button written into a TableCell, which both in-tree call sites do and which is what the compound shape exists to allow -- is a page-level tab stop Arena cannot silence, the same wall CalendarEvent's open panel hit and which its prompt documents as "the exception and is meant to be"; frameworks/react/test/table.test.jsx pins that as a second tab stop so the claim is verifiable rather than asserted. A binding CAN scope a requirement to a variant now -- `cases` exist, and `Skeleton` demonstrates that remedy rather than the limit it used to prove -- but this whole exception still reads as unconditional and is not, because Table was deliberately left flat. Its condition is not one of Table's own props: it depends on whether a CONSUMER put a click on a TableRow, and that is the third level of conditionality, which cases do not reach. Table also sits under the grid hand-test rule, so it can carry no render suite and any case it declared would be an unverified claim standing in for an accurate exception. Both reasons are recorded in CLAUDE.md's Known debt.
